script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for October 21, 2026.

script.heading: Story 2 - Eligibility for Early Mobilization in Mechanically Ventilated
sentences: Story 2 is about Eligibility for Early Mobilization in Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Multicenter Study..
This is a recent research article from Annals of the American Thoracic Society.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation for ≥4 hours across nine CLIF Consortium health systems (2018-2024) and MIMIC-IV (2008-2022), how should we interpret 3,281 hospitalizations, 86.9-95.6% met eligibility for mobilization within 72 hours of intubation across all 4 criteria compared with Chicago trials criteria, eligibility was reduced under TEAM (SHR 0.782, 95% CI 0.746-0.820) and Green (SHR 0.631, 0.611?
Among 223,281 hospitalizations, 86.9-95.6% met eligibility for mobilization within 72 hours of intubation across all 4 criteria.
Compared with Chicago trials criteria, eligibility was reduced under TEAM (SHR 0.782, 95% CI 0.746-0.820) and Green (SHR 0.631, 0.611-0.651) but not Yellow (SHR 0.990, 0.976-1.005).

Restricting eligibility to weekdays (structural) or requiring continuous eligibility (process) each reduced eligibility by 26-39% across all four criteria (SHR range 0.61-0.74); imposing both barriers together reduced eligibility by 45-56% (SHR range 0.44-0.55).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.

articles.title: Assessment of Tidal Volume in Patients Undergoing Noninvasive Ventilation: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: Observational studies of adults with ARF treated with NIV reporting Vt or Vt normalized to predicted body weight (Vt/PBW) in NIV success and failure groups. Eleven studies (1136 patients) were included. Vt/PBW was higher in NIV failure vs. success (mean difference [MD], 1.02 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.60-1.45 mL/kg]), whereas absolute Vt did not differ (MD, 1.30 [-33.31 to 35.91]). In hypoxemic ARF, Vt/PBW remained higher in NIV failure (MD, 0.89 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.04-1.73 mL/kg]); no data were available for hypercapnic ARF. Post hoc analyses showed that higher Vt/PBW was associated with increased mortality (odds ratio, 9.11; 95% CI, 3.88-21.37), higher respiratory rate (RR; MD, 3.14 breaths/min [95% CI, 1.36-4.92 breaths/min]), and lower Paco2 (MD, -2.38 mm Hg [95% CI, -4.16 to -0.5938 mm Hg]), but no with pressure support (PS) level (MD, 0.24 [95% CI, -0.81 to 1.29]).

articles.title: Eligibility for Early Mobilization in Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Multicenter Study.
articles.source: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.summary: Early mobilization of mechanically ventilated patients within 72 hours of intubation is underutilized despite its known clinical benefits. Retrospective cohort of adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation for ≥4 hours across nine CLIF Consortium health systems (2018-2024) and MIMIC-IV (2008-2022). Four physiologic eligibility criteria, from clinical trials (Chicago, TEAM) and consensus guidelines (Green, Yellow), were applied between 8am and 5pm within 72 hours of intubation. Among 223,281 hospitalizations, 86.9-95.6% met eligibility for mobilization within 72 hours of intubation across all 4 criteria. Compared with Chicago trials criteria, eligibility was reduced under TEAM (SHR 0.782, 95% CI 0.746-0.820) and Green (SHR 0.631, 0.611-0.651) but not Yellow (SHR 0.990, 0.976-1.005).
